title: Basilicata's Pumps Climb Past the National Average as Diesel Eases Off Its August Peak
dek: Self-service petrol in Italy's smallest mainland region has risen for seven straight readings, even as diesel quietly cools from a late-August high.
body: In Basilicata, self-service Benzina closed September 1st at €2.055 a litre and Gasolio at €2.171. Both sit above the national self-service averages of €2.035 and €2.161 respectively — Benzina running about 2 cents higher than the rest of Italy, Gasolio a more modest 1 cent above. For a region that often tracks close to the national line, this is a rare stretch where the local pump is the pricier one.

The two fuels are telling different stories right now. Benzina has risen in every one of the last seven tracked readings, up nearly a cent and a half since August 24th, with no sign yet of topping out. Gasolio, meanwhile, peaked on August 25th at €2.178 and has eased back gently ever since, settling almost seven-tenths of a cent lower by September 1st. On the ground, 268 stations are registered in Basilicata and 239 of them reported prices for the day — a reporting rate of roughly 89%, in line with the region's usual level of coverage.

Numbers this granular — a single region's day-by-day price history, station by station — would be tedious to track by hand in a spreadsheet, and stale within a week. caption:

Both sit above Italy's national self-service averages — a reminder that fuel prices don't move in lockstep even within one country.
